_README: Food content. Dish/experience names & descriptions are editorial (real). No invented prices or class durations — those vary by operator and are shown as 'check when you book'.

eat.d: Samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi grilled at your table, wrapped in lettuce with ssamjang and garlic.
Chewy rice cakes in sweet-spicy sauce, plus hotteok, gimbap and fish cakes from market stalls.
Rice bowl topped with vegetables, egg and gochujang — mix it all together before eating.
Extra-crispy fried chicken with beer — 'chimaek' is a national pastime.
Chewy buckwheat noodles in icy broth — a refreshing summer favorite.
Certified halal spots cluster around Itaewon; temple-food and veggie options are growing citywide.
Specialty coffee and creative desserts in Seoul's trendiest cafe district.
Bubbling stews like kimchi-jjigae and budae-jjigae — hearty and cheap.

make.d: Make and pack your own kimchi to take home; classes typically run with an English guide.
Cook a full Korean meal from scratch with a chef, then eat what you made.
Shape colorful traditional rice cakes — family-friendly and hands-on.
Learn to brew and taste Korean rice wine, usually with pairing snacks.

tips: A restaurant full of locals is usually a good sign.
Many places have picture menus or English menus; convenience stores are great for cheap late-night eats.
Side dishes (banchan) are free and often refillable.
For halal food, the Itaewon area has the most certified options.
Class prices and durations vary by operator — check the details when you book.
